{{infobox Chinese|l=Yin Metal Rooster|kanji=辛酉|romaji=kanoto tori|onyomi=shinyū|p=xīyǒu|w=hsin-yu|mi=ɕin⁵³ i̯ɤʊ̯²¹|y=san1 jau5|j=san1 jau5|ci=sɐn jɐu|mc=sin jɨu|oc-bs=sin jɯʔ}}
{{Sexagenary cycle}}
'''Yin Metal Rooster''' (辛酉, ''kanoto tori''; onyomi ''shinyū'') is the 58th of the sixty combinations of the {{ill|Sexagenary cycle|en|Sexagenary cycle|qid=Q246658|lt=Sexagenary cycle|1=Sexagenary cycle}}.

It is the 58th of the sixty stem-branch combinations, preceded by {{ill|Yang Metal Monkey|ja|庚申|1=Yang Metal Monkey}} and followed by {{ill|Yang Water Dog|ja|壬戌|1=Yang Water Dog}}. The {{ill|Heavenly Stems|en|Heavenly Stems|qid=Q1190985|lt=Heavenly Stem|1=Heavenly Stems}} ''辛'' is Yin Metal, and the {{ill|Earthly Branches|en|Earthly Branches|qid=Q1072961|lt=Earthly Branch|1=Earthly Branches}} ''酉'' (Rooster) is Yin Metal; together they form a Biwa (Mutual Harmony) relationship in {{ill|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|en|Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)|qid=Q218652|lt=Wuxing|1=Wuxing (Chinese philosophy)}}.

==Pronunciation==
* English: Yin Metal Rooster (辛酉)
** Chinese (Mandarin Pinyin): xīnyǒu
** Cantonese (Jyutping): san1 jau5
** Japanese:
***Kunyomi 1: Kanoto-tori
***Kunyomi 2: Shinkin-no-tori
***Onyomi 1: shinyuu
** Korean (Revised Romanization, Hangul): sinyu (신유)
** Vietnamese (Hán-Việt): Tân Dậu

==Years of Yin Metal Rooster==
{{Anchors|Xinyou Year}}
A {{ill|Common Era|en|Common Era|qid=Q208141|lt=Common Era|1=Common Era}} year that leaves a remainder of 1 when divided by 60 is a year of Yin Metal Rooster (辛酉).

Yin Metal Rooster is considered to have revolutionary significance.

In the ancient Chinese texts known as {{ill|Wei Shu|ja|緯書|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wei Shu|1=weishu|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q24890026}} (banned by Emperor {{ill|Emperor Yang of Sui|en|Emperor Yang of Sui|qid=Q7419|lt=Yang of Sui|1=Emperor Yang of Sui}}), with surviving fragments found in {{ill|Miyoshi Kiyotsura|en|Miyoshi Kiyotsura|qid=Q2399435|lt=Miyoshi Kiyoyuki|1=Miyoshi Kiyotsura}}’s “{{ill|Kakumei Kanbun|ja|革命勘文|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kakumei Kanbun|1=kakumei kanmon|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11663819}}” (collected in ''{{ill|Gunsho Ruijū|en|Gunsho Ruijū|qid=Q1554852|lt=Gunsho Ruijū|1=Gunsho Ruijū}}'' vol. 26), it is written that following {{ill|Kōshin|ja|庚申|1=Kōshin|lt=Yang Metal Monkey|2=ja|3=庚申|4=zh|5=庚申|6=ko|7=경신|lt_ko=경신|8=fr|9=Singe de métal|10=de|11=Metall-Affe|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōshin|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, Yin Metal Rooster also embodies the metal element, and Xin represents yin energy, often associated with people becoming cold-hearted. Thus, a Yin Metal Rooster year is considered a year when the {{ill|Mandate of Heaven|en|Mandate of Heaven|qid=Q875377|lt=Mandate of Heaven|1=Mandate of Heaven}} changes, marking revolutionary shifts in {{ill|Dynasty|en|Dynasty|qid=Q164950|lt=dynasties|1=Dynasty}}, known as the '''{{ill|Xinyou Revolution|ja|辛酉革命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Xinyou Revolution|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 辛酉|1=Yin Metal Rooster|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q904743}}'''.

In Japan, era name changes ({{ill|Era name|ja|改元|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Era name|1=era change|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11498853}}) during Yin Metal Rooster years were meant to prevent political upheaval. This practice started in Yin Metal Rooster of {{ill|901|en|901|qid=Q23580|lt=901|1=901}} ({{ill|Shōtai|en|Shōtai|qid=Q1324780|lt=Shōtai|1=Shōtai}} 4), when scholar-official Miyoshi Kiyoyuki proposed changing the era name to '''{{ill|Engi (era)|en|Engi (era)|qid=Q1374325|lt=Engi|1=Engi (era)}}'''. Frequently, era names were changed consecutively in both {{ill|Kōshin|ja|庚申|1=Kōshin|lt=Yang Metal Monkey|2=ja|3=庚申|4=zh|5=庚申|6=ko|7=경신|lt_ko=경신|8=fr|9=Singe de métal|10=de|11=Metall-Affe|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kōshin|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} and Yin Metal Rooster years, a custom that continued until the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji period|1=Meiji era}}, though such a precedent does not exist in China.

{{Anchors|Xinyou Revolution}}
During the Meiji era, scholar {{ill|Naka Michiyo|ja|那珂通世|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Naka Michiyo|1=Naka Michiyo|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11642793}} referenced ''Kakumei Kanbun'' with {{ill|Zheng Xuan|en|Zheng Xuan|qid=Q197649|lt=Zheng Xuan|1=Zheng Xuan}}’s annotation: 
* “The way of Heaven is not distant; after every three and five, it returns. Six cycles ({{ill|Wood Rat|en|Wood Rat|qid=Q1190890|lt=Yang Wood Rat|1=Yang Wood Rat}}) form one era, four sixes and two sixes overlap, and three sevens multiply to form 21 cycles, totaling 1,320 years.”
Based on this, it was believed that every '''1,260 years''' (21 cycles × 60 years = 1,260, called ''Ichibu'') there would be a major revolution during a Yin Metal Rooster year. Applying this, Naka theorized that the 9th year of {{ill|Empress Suiko|en|Empress Suiko|qid=Q298057|lt=Empress Suiko|1=Empress Suiko}}’s reign ({{ill|601|en|601|qid=Q30597|lt=601|1=601}}) marked such a revolutionary year, suggesting that Emperor {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|en|Emperor Jimmu|qid=Q200188|lt=Jimmu|1=Emperor Jimmu}}’s enthronement occurred 1,260 years earlier, in {{ill|660 BC|en|660 BC|qid=Q1059526|lt=660 BC|1=660 BC}}.

Alternatively, some interpret the annotation as indicating a '''1,320-year cycle''' (60 × 22 = 1,320). In this case, the pivotal year would shift to the year of the {{ill|Wood Rat|en|Wood Rat|qid=Q1190890|lt=Yang Wood Rat|1=Yang Wood Rat}}, three years after Yin Metal Rooster, considered the '''Jiazi Reform Year''' ({{ill|Jiazi Reform|ja|甲子革令|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jiazi Reform|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 甲子|1=Yang Wood Rat|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q1190890}}). This places the starting point at {{ill|664|en|664|qid=Q30621|lt=664|1=664}} AD, the year after the {{ill|Battle of Baekgang|en|Battle of Baekgang|qid=Q608727|lt=Battle of Baekgang|1=Battle of Baekgang}}, aligning with the legendary founding date of 660 BC.

==Months of Yin Metal Rooster==
A '''Yin Metal Rooster month''' occurs in {{ill|August|en|August|qid=Q122|lt=August|1=August}} of years ending in 3 or 8 (corresponding to Heavenly Stems {{ill|Gui|ja|癸|1=Mizunoto (癸)|lt=Mizunoto (癸)|2=ja|3=癸|4=zh|5=癸|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gui}} and {{ill|Wu|ja|戊|1=Tsuchinoe (戊)|lt=Tsuchinoe (戊)|2=ja|3=戊|4=zh|5=戊|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wu}}). Depending on the calendar system, this could refer to the {{ill|lunar calendar|ja|旧暦|1=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|11=Japanese Lunisolar Calendar|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/lunar calendar}} month or the solar term period between {{ill|Bailu (solar term)|en|Bailu (solar term)|qid=Q1191003|lt=White Dew|1=Bailu (solar term)}} and the day before {{ill|Hanlu|en|Hanlu|qid=Q1193124|lt=Cold Dew|1=Hanlu}}.

A '''Yin Metal Rooster day''' is the 7th day in the {{ill|Hassen|ja|八専|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hassen}} sequence, excluding intercalary days.
